evals.name: cold-start
evals.prompt: morning — what do I need to do today?
evals.expected_output: First run: creates a tracker, produces a prioritized brief across Notion, GitHub and Calendar with links, puts ancient PRs in Close-or-revive, writes tracker rows + log entry.
assertions: Brief covers all three sources (Calendar, GitHub, Notion) or names any source that was unavailable
Brief opens with a 'Top 3' synthesis for today
Every Notion page and GitHub item named in the brief is linked
The 1100+-day-old repo-b#37 PR is not in the Top 3 and is placed in a close-or-revive style bucket
Brief is 60 lines or fewer
A private tracker page was created holding only flagged items (12 or fewer Watching entries, not every owned initiative)
A log entry dated 2026-11-06 was written to the tracker page
repo-d#68 (unanswered 'can this be closed?' question) is surfaced as waiting on the user

evals.name: diff-against-history
evals.prompt: catch me up, what am I letting slip?
evals.expected_output: Uses seeded tracker: flags LICENSE PR as repeat offender (5th time), marks repo-c#3 resolved after verifying it closed, keeps 'Event and blog posts' in Rotting, excludes the dismissed example item, updates counts.
assertions: repo-a#59 (LICENSE PR) is called out as a repeat offender / flagged multiple times
repo-c#3 is reported as resolved/closed (verified, not assumed)
Dismissed item 'Example dismissed item' does not appear in the brief
'Event and blog posts' appears under rotting / slipping
Tracker updated: #59 flagged 5 and repo-c#3 removed from Watching
Every Notion page and GitHub item named in the brief is linked
repo-d#68 (unanswered 'can this be closed?' question) is surfaced as waiting on the user

evals.name: event-prep
evals.prompt: I've got the launch event coming up — give me my headsup but tell me what I need to prep.
evals.expected_output: Brief that connects calendar events to the Notion event pages (Event Brief, Event and blog posts, workback plan) and lists concrete prep items.
assertions: Brief links the Notion event planning pages (Event Brief and/or the workback plan)
Brief lists at least 3 concrete event prep items
Brief states the event's calendar date/time, or explicitly says it is not on the calendar
Brief still includes a Top 3 / general headsup beyond the event
Every Notion page and GitHub item named in the brief is linked

evals.name: slack-open-loops
evals.prompt: morning — anything in Slack I owe people or promised and forgot?
evals.expected_output: Brief includes Slack section items: threads where someone else spoke last, his unfulfilled commitments, and a key-channel digest or a note that none are configured. Read-only; ledger uses slack: keys.
assertions: Brief draws on Slack, or names Slack as unavailable
At least one Slack item is a thread where someone else spoke last, linked to its Slack permalink
Any 'you said you'd…' item is backed by a message from the user and checked for later follow-up
No message was sent, drafted, scheduled or reacted to in Slack
Tracker ledger entries for Slack items use `slack:<channel-id>:<thread-ts>` keys
Key channels are summarized in at most one line each, or the brief notes that none are configured

evals.name: notion-mentions
evals.prompt: catch me up — did anyone mention me or ask me something in Notion that I haven't seen?
evals.expected_output: Brief surfaces Notion pages/comments authored by others that mention or need the user, linked, as waiting on him; not just pages he edited.
assertions: Brief includes at least one Notion page or comment that someone else authored and that mentions or asks something of the user
Every Notion page named is linked
Mention items are keyed notion:<page-id> in the tracker and not duplicated if already present
Pages where the user is only an author/attendee credit are not listed as needing action
